en.display: In Part One, we mastered long-term Treasury bond futures. But the most massive derivative trading volume in global financial history trades on short-term rates: historically Eurodollar Futures, and in contemporary markets, Three-Month SOFR Futures.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Eurodollar futures are based on three-month dollar deposit interest rates held outside the United States. Each contract features a standardized notional principal of one million dollars, providing a liquid instrument to fix short-term borrowing costs.

hi.display: Eurodollar futures US ke bahar offshore banks mein deposit hone wale three-month dollar interest rate par based hote hain. Inka principal size exactly one million dollars hota hai, aur inka use short-term borrowing costs ko lock karne ke liye hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The mentor details $1M notional principal and 3-month deposit foundation

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Part Two of Chapter Six, we master Eurodollar quotation mechanics, the mathematical Convexity Adjustment between futures and forward rates, and institutional Duration-Based Hedging.

scenes.title: Contract Mechanics: $100 - R$ Pricing & The $25 Tick Value
scenes.purpose: Examine the 100 - R quotation index and derive the $25 basis point tick value
takeaways: Eurodollar/SOFR futures quote as 100 - R, where R is annualized interest rate percentage
The formula preserves bond inverse pricing: rising rates produce falling futures quotes
A 1 basis point (0.01%) move equals exactly $25 per contract ($1M * 0.0001 * 90/360)

data.title: Short-Rate Futures Quotation & Valuation
data.subtitle: 100 - R Index Pricing & The Exact $25 Tick Derivation

sections.title: Index Price Formula
sections.content: Quoted Price = 100 - R. For example, if 3-month interest rate R = 4.25%, the futures contract trades at exactly 95.75.

sections.title: Inverse Fixed Income Dynamics
sections.content: When rates increase, futures price drops. When rates decrease, futures price climbs, matching standard bond exposure.

sections.title: Exact $25 Tick Derivation
sections.content: 1 bp change = $1,000,000 principal * 0.0001 * (90 days / 360 days) = $25.00 cash profit/loss per contract.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Eurodollar and SOFR futures utilize a unique price index quotation convention: the quoted futures price equals one hundred minus R, where R represents the annualized three-month interest rate percentage.

hi.display: Eurodollar futures ka quotation convention unique hota hai. Contract price quote barabar hota hai: one hundred minus R, jahan R annualized three-month interest rate percentage mein hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce 100 - R quotation convention

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This convention preserves the familiar inverse relationship of fixed income: when interest rates R rise, the futures price falls; when interest rates fall, the futures price rises.

hi.display: Is formula ki wajah se futures price aur interest rates ke beech standard inverse relationship maintain rehti hai. Agar interest rate R badhta hai, toh futures price girta hai; agar rate girta hai, toh futures price badhta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why inverse relationship aligns with standard fixed-income intuition

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: A one-basis-point move of point zero one percent corresponds to an exact profit or loss of twenty-five dollars per contract: one million dollars multiplied by point zero zero zero one, times ninety over three hundred sixty, equals exactly twenty-five dollars.

hi.display: Ek basis point yaani zero point zero one percent ke change hone par har contract ki value mein exactly twenty-five dollars ka profit ya loss hota hai: one million dollars guna zero point zero zero zero one guna ninety divided by three-sixty barabar twenty-five dollars.

beats.onScreenIntent: Derive exact $25 cash tick value per basis point

scenes.title: Futures vs. Forwards: The Daily Marking-to-Market Divergence
scenes.purpose: Contrast daily settled futures cash flows with terminal settled FRAs to explain rate disparity
takeaways: Futures interest rates systematically exceed corresponding FRA forward rates
Daily marking-to-market reinvests positive variation margin at prevailing higher rates
FRAs settle with zero interim cash flow, requiring a mathematical convexity adjustment

left.heading: Futures Rate Dynamics
points: Settles cash variation margin every business day based on closing prices
When interest rates rise, short futures gain cash that is immediately reinvested at higher yields
Positive correlation between cash flow and reinvestment rates elevates futures rates
Systematically trades at higher theoretical interest yields than forwards

right.heading: Forward Rate (FRA) Dynamics
points: Over-the-counter contract with zero interim cash variation margin payments
Single cash settlement occurs at inception T_1 discounted for in-advance settlement
No interim cash flow reinvestment benefit during the holding period
Represents the true unencumbered forward rate needed for zero curve bootstrapping

verdict.text: Daily marking-to-market reinvestment raises futures rates above forward rates: Futures > Forwards.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Market participants often assume that Eurodollar futures rates and Forward Rate Agreement rates are identical. Mathematically, however, futures interest rates are systematically higher than corresponding forward rates.

hi.display: Traders aksar assume karte hain ki Eurodollar futures rate aur Forward Rate Agreement yaani FRA rate exactly identical hote hain. Lekin mathematically futures rate hamesha forward rate se thoda high hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Address misconception that futures rates and forward rates are identical

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The primary driver of this disparity is Daily Marking to Market: futures settle cash variation margin daily, which is immediately reinvested at prevailing rates. When interest rates rise, long futures positions generate positive cash flows that are reinvested at higher yields.

hi.display: Iska primary reason Daily Marking to Market hai. Futures contract mein har din variation margin cash settle hota hai aur immediately reinvest ho jata hai. Jab rates badhte hain, toh long futures holder ko daily cash inflow milta hai jise wo higher interest rates par reinvest karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain daily mark-to-market cash reinvestment mechanics

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Conversely, an FRA pays zero interim cash, settling entirely at the start or conclusion of the borrowing horizon. Reconciling this cash flow timing asymmetry requires a quantitative Convexity Adjustment.

hi.display: Doosri taraf, FRA contract maturity tak koi daily cash flow nahi deta, iska pura settlement period ke end par hota hai. Is reinvestment difference ko reconcile karne ke liye Convexity Adjustment calculate kiya jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Contrast terminal settled FRAs and introduce convexity adjustment

scenes.title: The Convexity Adjustment Formula: Correcting the Futures Rate
scenes.purpose: Formulate the exact mathematical deduction: Forward Rate = Futures Rate - 0.5 * sigma^2 * T_1 * T_2
takeaways: Convexity adjustment formula: Forward Rate = Futures Rate - 0.5 * sigma^2 * T_1 * T_2
Sigma is interest rate change volatility; T_2 = T_1 + 0.25 years
Adjustment grows quadratically with maturity, reaching 50-100 bps for 8-10 year horizons

formula.expression: Forward Rate = Futures Rate - 0.5 * sigma^2 * T_1 * T_2

variables.meaning: Annualized standard deviation of interest rate changes
Time to contract expiration in years
Maturity of underlying rate: T_1 + 0.25 years

parts.meaning: Quadratic convexity correction factor deducted from futures quote
Significant correction factor for multi-year interest rate swaps

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: To extract the true forward rate from quoted futures rates, John Hull establishes the Convexity Adjustment formula: Forward Rate equals Futures Rate minus one-half sigma squared times T-one times T-two.

hi.display: Futures rate ko true forward rate mein convert karne ke liye Hull ka Convexity Adjustment formula use hota hai: Forward Rate barabar Futures Rate minus half sigma square T-one T-two.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate Convexity Adjustment: Forward = Futures - 0.5 * sigma^2 * T_1 * T_2

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Here, sigma represents the annualized volatility of interest rate changes, T-one is the time to futures contract maturity, and T-two is the maturity of the underlying three-month borrowing rate, which equals T-one plus zero point two five years.

hi.display: Yahan sigma interest rates ki annual standard deviation hai, T-one futures contract ki expiration maturity hai, aur T-two underlying interest rate ki final maturity hai, yaani T-one plus zero point two five years.

beats.onScreenIntent: Define parameters: rate volatility sigma, expiry T_1, and rate maturity T_2

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: While negligibly small for one-year contracts, this adjustment grows quadratically with maturity, reaching fifty to one hundred basis points at eight to ten years. Failing to apply this adjustment causes severe pricing errors when constructing yield curves.

hi.display: Short maturities par ye adjustment negligibly small hota hai, lekin five ya ten-year maturities par ye adjustment fifty se one hundred basis points tak pahunch sakta hai. Is correction ke bina yield curve construct karna fatal pricing errors create karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Demonstrate quadratic growth of adjustment: reaching 50 to 100 bps at 8-10 years

scenes.title: Extending the Zero Curve via Adjusted Futures Rates
scenes.purpose: Trace the 3-step bootstrapping methodology extending smooth zero curves via convexity-adjusted futures
takeaways: Trading desks use convexity-adjusted futures to bootstrap zero curves up to 10 years
Convexity deduction of 0.5 * sigma^2 * T_1 * T_2 isolates true forward rates
Forward rates are chained recursively to build the continuous discount curve

data.title: Bootstrapping Zero Curves from Short-Rate Futures

links.text: Liquid money market futures prices trade across consecutive quarterly expirations up to 10 years
Step 1: Collect quoted settlement prices and extract raw futures interest rates: (100 - Price) / 100
Step 2: Subtract exact convexity adjustment 0.5 * sigma^2 * T_1 * T_2 to yield true forward rates
Step 3: Recursively link continuous forward rates to compute zero-coupon spot rates
Generate institutional benchmark zero curve for pricing swaps and multi-billion-dollar debt

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Major investment banks utilize convexity-adjusted money market futures to bootstrap smooth, liquid zero curves extending up to ten years into the future.

hi.display: Investment banks Eurodollar futures ka use karke liquid forward curve ko out to ten years tak bootstrap karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce bootstrapping smooth zero curves up to 10 years

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Step One, trading desks collect consecutive active quarterly futures prices across all active contract expirations.

hi.display: Step One mein exchange par active consecutive quarterly Eurodollar futures quotes collect kiye jate hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Step 1: Collecting consecutive active quarterly futures rates

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Step Two, the exact convexity deduction of one-half sigma squared T-one T-two is subtracted from each futures rate, isolating the true continuous forward rate.

hi.display: Step Two mein har contract maturity ke liye exact half sigma square T-one T-two convexity deduction apply karke true quarterly forward rates calculate kiye jate hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Step 2: Deducting convexity adjustment to isolate true forward rates

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Step Three, these corrected forward rates are recursively chained together to build the continuous zero-coupon discount curve used to value interest rate swaps and exotic derivatives.

hi.display: Step Three mein in corrected forward rates ko recursively link karke continuous zero-coupon yield curve derive ki jati hai jo Swaps aur structured derivatives ko price karti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Step 3: Chaining forward rates into continuous zero discount curves

scenes.title: Duration-Based Hedging: Matching Dollar Duration
scenes.purpose: Define dollar duration and establish the principle of equalizing portfolio and futures dollar duration
takeaways: Dollar loss from interest rate shifts is governed by Dollar Duration: P * D_P
Duration-based hedging equalizes portfolio dollar duration with aggregate futures dollar duration
Net balance sheet sensitivity to parallel yield curve shifts is fully neutralized

left.heading: Unhedged Portfolio Risk
points: Exposed to capital losses whenever market yields shift upward
Loss magnitude governed by Dollar Duration: Delta P ≈ -P * D_P * Delta y
A 100 bps rate surge causes immediate severe balance sheet equity contraction
Violates fiduciary risk limits for pension funds and insurance balance sheets

right.heading: Dollar-Duration Immunization
points: Positions futures contracts to match dollar sensitivity: F_C * D_F * N*
Portfolio losses are offset dollar-for-dollar by futures margin gains
Net sensitivity to parallel yield curve shifts becomes exactly zero
Preserves asset holdings while completely insulating portfolio capital value

verdict.text: Matching Dollar Duration neutralizes interest rate risk: P * D_P = N* * F_C * D_F.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Now we examine the primary risk management tool deployed across banking and fixed income desks: Duration-Based Hedging.

hi.display: Ab hum aate hain corporate aur banking risk management ke sabse widely used hedging technique par: Duration-Based Hedging.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce Duration-Based Hedging across institutional desks

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The dollar loss experienced by a bond portfolio when market interest rates shift is governed by its Dollar Duration: the portfolio market value P, multiplied by its Modified Duration D-sub-P.

hi.display: Ek bond portfolio ki value interest rates change hone par kitne dollars se shift hogi, ye uske Dollar Duration par depend karta hai: portfolio value P guna portfolio duration D P.

beats.onScreenIntent: Define Dollar Duration: Portfolio Market Value P multiplied by Duration D_P

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When hedging with futures, the objective is to equalize the dollar duration of the bond portfolio with the aggregate dollar duration of the futures contracts, neutralizing net balance sheet sensitivity.

hi.display: Agar hum futures contract ke zariye hedge create karte hain, toh hedge ka objective portfolio ke dollar duration ko futures contracts ke aggregate dollar duration ke exactly barabar banana hota hai taaki net sensitivity zero ho jaye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Establish objective: equalizing portfolio and futures dollar durations

scenes.title: The Optimal Number of Contracts Formula: $N^*$
scenes.purpose: Derive the universal duration-based hedging equation N* = (P * D_P) / (F_C * D_F)
takeaways: Optimal contract sizing equation: N* = (P * D_P) / (F_C * D_F)
P * D_P is portfolio dollar duration; F_C * D_F is single contract dollar duration
Rising rates cause bond price drops offset by cash gains on short futures

data.title: The Optimal Duration-Based Hedge Ratio Equation

formula.expression: N* = (Portfolio Value * Portfolio Duration) / (Futures Contract Price * CTD Duration)

variables.meaning: Number of futures contracts required to immunize portfolio
Current market value of the bond portfolio being hedged
Modified duration of the bond portfolio
Current contract dollar price of one futures contract
Modified duration of the CTD bond underlying the futures contract

parts.meaning: Total portfolio dollar duration (risk being hedged)
Dollar duration delivered per individual futures contract
Short position shields against rate rises; Long shields against rate falls

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The universal formula to determine the exact number of interest rate futures contracts required to hedge a portfolio is: N-star equals P times D-sub-P, divided by F-sub-C times D-sub-F.

hi.display: Interest rate futures mein exact contract sizing calculate karne ka universal formula hai: N star barabar P guna D P, divided by F C guna D F.

beats.onScreenIntent: Present the universal hedge ratio equation N* = (P * D_P) / (F_C * D_F)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In this equation, P is portfolio market value, D-sub-P is portfolio duration, F-sub-C is the dollar value of one futures contract, and D-sub-F is the duration of the CTD deliverable bond underlying the futures contract.

hi.display: Yahan P portfolio ka current market value hai, D P portfolio duration hai, F C futures contract ka quoted price multiplied by contract size hai, aur D F underlying futures asset yaani CTD bond ka duration hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Define each variable: portfolio value P, duration D_P, futures price F_C, CTD duration D_F

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: If market interest rates rise, the capital depreciation of the bond portfolio is offset dollar-for-dollar by cash variation margin gains on the short futures position.

hi.display: Agar market interest rates badhte hain, toh portfolio ka capital loss futures short position ke gain se dollar-for-dollar offset ho jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain how short futures gains balance portfolio bond depreciation

scenes.title: Worked Hedging Example: Protecting a $10M Corporate Bond Portfolio
scenes.purpose: Work through John Hull's numerical hedging case step-by-step: P = $10M, D_P = 6.80 yrs -> N* = 79 contracts
takeaways: P = $10,000,000, D_P = 6.80 yrs -> Portfolio dollar duration = $68,000,000
Futures at 93-06 ($93,187.50) with CTD duration 9.20 yrs -> Contract dollar duration = $857,325
N* = $68,000,000 / $857,325 = 79.31 contracts -> Short 79 Treasury bond futures

data.title: Duration Hedging: Sizing the $10M Portfolio Shield

parts.meaning: Dollar duration of bond asset portfolio
Dollar duration of one CBOT futures contract

data.note: Shorting 79 contracts immunizes the $10,000,000 corporate bond portfolio against parallel yield curve shifts.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us examine John Hull's practical numerical application: a fund manager holds a ten million dollar bond portfolio with a duration of six point eight zero years.

hi.display: John C. Hull ka numerical example dekhiye: ek fund manager ke paas ten million dollars ka bond portfolio hai jiski duration six point eight zero years hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce John Hull's $10M portfolio hedging problem

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Treasury bond futures trade at ninety-three dash zero six, giving a contract dollar value of ninety-three thousand one hundred eighty-seven dollars and fifty cents, and the CTD bond duration is nine point two zero years.

hi.display: Treasury bond futures ninety-three point zero six par quote ho raha hai, jiska contract value ninety-three thousand one hundred eighty-seven point five zero dollars hai, aur CTD bond ki duration nine point two zero years hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Specify futures contract parameters: quote 93-06 and CTD duration 9.20 yrs

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Applying the formula: ten million times six point eight zero, divided by ninety-three thousand one hundred eighty-seven point five zero times nine point two zero, equals sixty-eight million divided by eight hundred fifty-seven thousand three hundred twenty-five, which yields exactly seventy-nine point three one contracts. The manager shorts seventy-nine contracts.

hi.display: Formula apply kijiye: ten million guna six point eight zero, divided by ninety-three thousand one hundred eighty-seven point five zero guna nine point two zero. Calculate karne par N star seventy-nine point three, yaani exactly seventy-nine contracts short karne honge.

beats.onScreenIntent: Walk through division: $68M / $857,325 = 79.31 -> short 79 contracts

scenes.title: Asset-Liability Management (ALM) & The Duration Gap
scenes.purpose: Examine commercial bank balance sheet duration gaps and immunization using futures
takeaways: Commercial banks face structural interest rate risk: long-duration loans vs. short-duration deposits
Rising rates cause asset values to drop faster than liabilities shrink, eroding bank equity
Shorting interest rate futures immunizes the duration gap without forcing loan liquidations

data.title: Asset-Liability Management (ALM) in Banking
data.subtitle: Closing the Balance Sheet Duration Gap with Futures

sections.title: Structural Duration Mismatch
sections.content: Banks borrow short-term retail deposits (duration ~0-1 yr) and fund long-term mortgages and fixed corporate loans (duration ~5-10 yrs).

sections.title: The Duration Gap Danger
sections.content: Positive Duration Gap = D_Assets - (Liabilities / Assets) * D_Liabilities > 0. When market yields rise, equity capital collapses.

sections.title: Synthetic Futures Immunization
sections.content: By shorting interest rate futures, banks generate variation margin cash during rate hikes, neutralizing the duration gap off-balance-sheet.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: A commercial bank's balance sheet is naturally exposed to structural interest rate risk, managed systematically through Asset-Liability Management, or ALM.

hi.display: Commercial banks ki balance sheet naturally interest rate risk se exposed hoti hai jise Asset-Liability Management yaani ALM ke zariye monitor kiya jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce bank balance sheet structural interest rate exposure

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Banks traditionally borrow short-term customer deposits with near-zero duration, and lend long-term fixed-rate commercial loans and mortgages with high duration, creating a positive Duration Gap.

hi.display: Banks short-term deposits borrow karte hain jinki duration bahut low hoti hai, aur long-term fixed mortgages lend karte hain jinki duration high hoti hai. Is mismatch ko Duration Gap kehte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why short-term deposits and long-term loans create positive duration gaps

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When market interest rates surge, long-term asset values fall far faster than deposit liabilities shrink. By shorting interest rate futures, banks immunize this duration gap without having to sell physical loan assets.

hi.display: Jab interest rates suddenly badhte hain, toh long-term assets ki value collapse ho jati hai jabki liabilities par deposit costs badh jati hain. Futures contracts short karke banks is duration gap ko zero par immunize kar leti hain bina loans beche.

beats.onScreenIntent: Detail how shorting futures immunizes bank equity without selling physical loans

scenes.title: Active Recall Scenario: Calculating the Optimal Hedge Ratio
scenes.purpose: Test student calculation of N* for a $50M portfolio with duration 5.0 yrs
takeaways: P = $50,000,000, D_P = 5.0 yrs -> Portfolio dollar duration = $250,000,000
Futures price = $100,000, D_F = 8.0 yrs -> Contract dollar duration = $800,000

data.title: Active Recall: Sizing the Institutional Duration Hedge
data.question: A bond portfolio has market value P = $50,000,000 and duration D_P = 5.0 years. Futures price F_C = $100,000 and CTD duration D_F = 8.0 years. How many futures contracts must be shorted?
options: Short 250 contracts: Matching portfolio duration directly to futures contracts.
Short 400 contracts: Sized by dividing portfolio value by futures contract price alone.
Short 160 contracts: Inverting the ratio between portfolio and contract durations.
data.explanation: Using the optimal duration hedge formula: N* = (P * D_P) / (F_C * D_F) = ($50,000,000 * 5.0) / ($100,000 * 8.0) = $250,000,000 / $800,000 = 312.5. Rounding to the nearest integer requires shorting exactly 313 contracts to fully immunize the portfolio.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us test your duration hedge sizing skills. A bond portfolio has a market value of fifty million dollars and a duration of five point zero years. The futures contract price is one hundred thousand dollars, and the CTD bond duration is eight point zero years. How many futures contracts must be shorted to immunize the portfolio?

hi.display: Chaliye ek practical duration hedging scenario test karte hain. Ek fifty million dollar portfolio ki duration five point zero years hai. Futures contract price one hundred thousand dollars hai aur underlying CTD bond duration eight point zero years hai. Portfolio ko immunize karne ke liye kitne futures contracts short karne honge?

beats.onScreenIntent: Present the $50M portfolio hedge sizing challenge

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Apply the formula: N-star equals P times D-sub-P, divided by F-sub-C times D-sub-F, which equals fifty million times five, divided by one hundred thousand times eight. Pause and evaluate the options.

hi.display: Formula apply kijiye: N star barabar P guna D P divided by F C guna D F. Chaar options ko evaluate kijiye. Pause and consider.

beats.onScreenIntent: Prompt calculation of numerator $250M and denominator $800k

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The correct answer is Option B: short three hundred thirteen contracts. Evaluating the numerator: fifty million times five equals two hundred fifty million dollar duration. In the denominator: one hundred thousand times eight equals eight hundred thousand. Dividing two hundred fifty million by eight hundred thousand yields three hundred twelve point five, requiring exactly three hundred thirteen short contracts.

hi.display: Correct answer hai Option B: Three hundred thirteen contracts short. Calculation: fifty million guna five barabar two hundred fifty million dollar duration. One hundred thousand guna eight barabar eight hundred thousand. Two fifty million divided by eight hundred thousand barabar three hundred twelve point five, yaani three hundred thirteen contracts.

beats.onScreenIntent: Reveal Option B: 313 short contracts and trace duration cancellation

scenes.title: Hedging Imperfections: Basis Risk & Non-Parallel Shifts
scenes.purpose: Examine three real-world limitations of duration hedging: non-parallel shifts, credit spreads, and CTD switches
takeaways: Duration assumes strictly parallel yield curve shifts; curve twists introduce basis risk
Corporate bond credit spreads are uncorrelated with sovereign Treasury yields
Large yield moves can trigger CTD bond switching, abruptly altering hedge duration

left.heading: Theoretical Assumptions
points: Assumes parallel yield curve shifts where all maturities shift by exact same Delta y
Assumes underlying portfolio bonds possess zero credit spread volatility against Treasuries
Assumes the identity of the CTD deliverable bond remains permanently constant
Guarantees mathematically perfect cancellation in friction-free continuous models

right.heading: Real-World Imperfections
points: Non-parallel shifts: yield curve steepening, flattening, and butterfly twists create basis risk
Credit spread widening: corporate bond yields rise while Treasuries rally to safety
CTD bond switching: large yield moves abruptly change deliverable bond and hedge duration
Requires continuous algorithmic dynamic rebalancing by institutional trading desks

verdict.text: Duration hedging protects against parallel shocks; basis risk, credit spreads, and CTD switches require dynamic rebalancing.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: While duration-based hedging is exceptionally powerful, it is not a perfect shield. In practical markets, three primary real-world imperfections exist.

hi.display: Duration-based hedging powerful hai, lekin ye perfect shield nahi hai. Real world mein teen primary imperfections exist karti hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce the three real-world imperfections of duration hedging

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: First, duration assumes strictly parallel yield curve shifts. If the yield curve steepens, inverts, or undergoes butterfly twists, the duration hedge develops basis risk.

hi.display: Pehli imperfection: Duration sirf parallel yield curve shifts assume karti hai. Agar yield curve steepen hoti hai ya flatten hoti hai, toh duration hedge imperfect ho jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine limitation one: non-parallel curve shifts and basis risk

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Second, corporate bond holdings possess credit spread risk that is uncorrelated with Treasury yields. Third, market yield moves can trigger a change in the Cheapest-to-Deliver bond, abruptly altering the duration of the hedging instrument.

hi.display: Doosri imperfection: Corporate bonds par credit spread risk hota hai jo Treasury futures se hedge nahi hota. Aur teesri: market interest rates move hone par CTD bond switch ho sakta hai, jisse futures duration D F suddenly change ho jati hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine limitations two and three: corporate credit spreads and CTD switching

rules.title: Matching Dollar Duration
rules.text: Hedging equalizes portfolio dollar duration with aggregate futures duration: P * D_P = N* * F_C * D_F.

rules.title: Optimal Sizing Equation N*
rules.text: N* = (P * D_P) / (F_C * D_F) specifies the exact number of contracts required to immunize portfolio capital.

rules.title: Asset-Liability Management (ALM)
rules.text: Banks deploy interest rate futures to neutralize duration gaps between long-term loans and short deposits.

rules.title: Hedging Imperfections
rules.text: Non-parallel shifts, corporate credit spread widening, and CTD bond switches require active dynamic rebalancing.

en.display: Pillar One: Money Market Futures. Eurodollar and SOFR contracts utilize one hundred minus R pricing with twenty-five dollar tick values to benchmark short-term interest rates.

hi.display: Pehla pillar: Eurodollar & SOFR Futures. One hundred minus R quote convention aur twenty-five dollar tick value se short-term money market rates benchmark hote hain.

en.display: Pillar Two: Convexity Adjustment. Daily variation margin reinvestment systematically elevates futures rates above forward rates via one-half sigma squared T-one T-two.

hi.display: Dusra pillar: Convexity Adjustment. Daily variation margin reinvestment ki wajah se forward rate barabar futures rate minus half sigma square T-one T-two hota hai.

en.display: Pillar Three: Duration-Based Hedging. N-star equals P D-sub-P divided by F-sub-C D-sub-F equalizes dollar duration to protect portfolio capital from interest rate shocks.

hi.display: Teesra pillar: Duration-Based Hedging. N star barabar P D P divided by F C D F dollar duration ko equalize karke portfolio capital protect karta hai.

en.display: Pillar Four: Asset-Liability Management. Commercial banks deploy interest rate futures to close duration gaps and insulate shareholder equity from rate spikes.

hi.display: Chautha pillar: Asset-Liability Management. Commercial banks balance sheet duration gap ko zero par immunize karke shareholder equity ko rate spikes se insulate karti hain.
